newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Optus dealing plans not to be revoked - ACCC.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Optus dealing plans not to be revoked - ACCC.

text.p: The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) said on Monday that it would not revoke two Third Line Forcing Exclusive Dealing Arrangements notified by the Optus group of companies.
Third line forcing occurs where the acquisition of one company's services may require the consumer to also take another company's services.
The most common example is the "bundling" of services and products.
In a statement, the ACCC said the one notification related to the bundling by Optus Vision, Optus' part-owned pay TV unit, of pay TV services and local telephony.
Optus Communications is Australia's second largest telecommunications network.
Optus Vision is offering free installation for pay TV services conditional on consumers acquiring Optus local telephony services.

The other notifications related to mobile and long distance telephony services bundling where mobile services were offered for free trials or discounts conditional on consumers acquiring Optus long distance services.
ACCC chairman Allan Fels said as Optus did not have substantial market shares in the relevant markets, allowing the deals would not be detrimental to market information or consumer choice.

"The ACCC considered the conduct would not be detrimental to market information available to consumers on the individual prioducts, or on consumer choice. Consumers will not be forced to take two products and will be free to buy the services from either Optus or its competitors," Fels said.

Optus Communications owns 46.5 percent of Optus Vision as does Continental CableVision Inc, which is currently merging with U.S. West. Seven Network Ltd and Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd own the remainder.
Optus Communication's shareholders include Mayne Nickless Ltd, BellSouth Corp and Cable and Wireless Plc, which each hold about one-quarter of the company.
